Completed-batch changes: 1→2 +1.00 pp; 2→3 +2.00 pp; 3→5 +57.33 pp. First-to-latest relative accuracy increase: 229.11% (3.29× the initial accuracy); observed error-rate reduction: 81.90%. These describe the trend across different samples, not measured causal improvements. Serpent's finite inventory lost exhausted families over time; the latest batch covers only six families. The latest transport change coincided with the largest increase but has no paired end-to-end effect measurement.

Five batches reserved 1,500 unique sentences. Batch 4 stopped after four completed failures; its remaining 296 have no scored result and are not counted as wrong or successfully evaluated. One interrupted call may have reached the model but has no completed record. All 300 batch-4 sentences were retired from future fresh selection.

With the earlier 50-sentence experiment included, each repeated sentence is counted once for unique totals. “Ever correct” means at least one saved scored attempt was correct; it is not an accuracy estimate for today's reader. Earlier smoke/pilot runs use a different review format, so their unique encounters are counted separately and their judgments are not merged into exact-slot accuracy. No repository log can establish lifetime or pretraining exposure.

Rules ranked by measured help — ascending

Only two individual rules have comparable paired measurements. The AI answers were held fixed while the candidate binding changed. These are verified binding recoveries, not new end-to-end model runs. Together they recovered 11 distinct cases, 79→90/300 (+3.67 pp), with zero regressions.

Evidence and limits
Compiled from saved cases.jsonl, summary.json, abort.json, offline-audit.json, fixes.json and development-binding files in the Kobra workspace. This HTML contains its own data and works offline. No benchmark or reader source was changed. No additional model calls were made.
The scored contract covers 11 source-surface slots. It does not score the complete Serpent meaning graph, every relation, or conversational recovery by ASK. No claims are made about unseen grammar structures or pretraining. Batch 2 had a failed preflight test that was documented in its erratum and fixed later; it must not be described as having passed all preflight tests.
